strategies.desc: Performs 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, where each iteration computes data-dependent factors from the previous result before launching the next all-reduce. This is the reference approach with 8 all-reduce dispatches (9 total including initial sum). Trades maximum dispatch count for simplest correctness guarantee and minimal local buffer usage.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapped computation-communication
strategies.desc: Restructure to overlap local computation (squaring, mean, factor calculation) with in-flight all-reduce operations by splitting blocks and pre-computing factors where possible. Uses async dispatch patterns to hide latency of 8 all-reduce operations by interleaving computation of independent blocks' statistics. Same 8-9 dispatches but improved wall-clock time through better parallelism.

strategies.name: Batched all-reduce with chunked payloads
strategies.desc: Pack multiple transformed blocks into a single larger payload and dispatch fewer all-reduce operations (potentially 4 batched instead of 8 individual). Each batch carries 2 iterations' worth of transformed data, trading larger per-dispatch payload size for reduced dispatch overhead. Requires careful buffering to maintain data-dependency correctness.

strategies.name: Ring-based reduce-scatter then all-gather
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pattern, allowing partial results to be computed locally during the scatter phase. For 8 iterations this gives 16 collective dispatches but each operates on 1/world_size payload, potentially better bandwidth utilization at world_size=224. Trades dispatch count for per-dispatch message size reduction.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology by first performing node-local reductions (assuming multiple devices per node), then inter-node all-reduce, followed by intra-node broadcast. For 8 dependent iterations, uses approximately 8×3 = 24 dispatches but each inter-node operation moves data across fewer network hops. Optimizes for multi-node bandwidth hierarchy at the cost of more total collectives.
